spec.behavior: Serve a long-lived line-oriented TCP worker service. `ready` reports readiness, `batch N` queues values 1 through N through four workers and returns their square sum, and `shutdown` returns goodbye then exits cleanly.

jet.author: luna-max
jet.notes: Long-lived raw TCP line service; starts four persistent workers over bounded channels, then queues each batch through that pool.

go.author: luna-max
go.notes: Stdlib TCP listener and four-worker channel.

rust.author: luna-max
rust.notes: Std-only TCP listener, sync channel, and four worker threads.

python.author: luna-max
python.notes: Stdlib socket listener and four worker threads.

node.author: luna-max
node.notes: Added a built-in Node net listener with four asynchronous workers and the same line protocol.

rewrite_provenance.changed: No source rewrite: run.jet already uses the ratified #CLI entry, bounded channel<T>(capacity: ...), task.group(limit: ...), fenced four-worker spawn, canonical ranges, and core.net/core.time stream APIs. Retained the source because available alternatives would add a job/result carrier or change input and failure behavior without simplifying the canonical program.
rewrite_provenance.matched: Same long-lived TCP line protocol as Go, Rust, Python, and Node: ready, batch N for values 1 through N, square results summed in receive order, bounded four-worker queue, shutdown, clean worker join, and exact response formatting; no input, side effect, ordering, or output work was removed.
